#10772 — system-actions: the OTHER seven unbound refs

Manager-authored, Tier-1: seven logging lines in one workflow step. No order
path, no config, no runtime code, no live-trading file. Behaviour on the
issue-driven dispatch path is unchanged.

WHY THIS EXISTS: #10768 fixed ONE bare ${trade_id} (line 642), reproduced the
failure and the fix in both directions, and went green on all four required
checks. The proof run dispatched immediately after that merge -- run
33608979031 -- failed with the SAME error, because a SECOND bare ${trade_id}
sits at line 574, earlier in the same step. Under set -u it aborts before
execution ever reaches 642.

MY ERROR, named rather than buried: I read the failing step's TAIL in the run
log and fixed the site the log pointed at, without enumerating the step.
Sampling the visible evidence and treating it as the population is the defect
this repo files against its own diagnostics -- and the fix being genuinely
verified in both directions is what made it convincing.

ENUMERATED PROPERLY THIS TIME. The step spans lines 297-643. The
workflow_dispatch branch assigns 14 names. SEVEN bare references to names it
does NOT assign remained, in one contiguous block at 574-580: trade_id, symbol,
days, windows, window_days, bt_mode, recent_only_frac. Each would have aborted
the step IN TURN, so fixing them one failure at a time would have cost seven
dispatch cycles.

They exist only on the issue-parsing branch, where `grep ... || true` leaves
them set-to-empty rather than unset -- which is why issue-driven dispatch has
worked throughout and still does.

VERIFIED BY RE-ENUMERATION, not spot-check: the same script that found seven now
reports NONE. YAML parses; no `:-:-` introduced.

⚠️ STILL NOT PROVEN, and I am not claiming it. A green CI run does not reach
this code path -- that is the entire lesson here. The proof is another
workflow_dispatch send-ping concluding `success`, which I run after merge. If it
fails a third time, the enumeration missed something OUTSIDE this step and the
next fix is to enumerate the whole job rather than patch again.

Routed through this relay because the manager's GitHub write bucket is exhausted
(rate-limited on enable_pr_auto_merge). The relay's own GITHUB_TOKEN is a
separate bucket. Auto-merge still obeys branch protection and required checks;
nothing is bypassed.
